goal: Extract private protocol-related helper methods from Safelist into a small, cohesive helper class to reduce Safelist size and concentrate protocol-specific logic.

ops.details: Create new class org.jsoup.safety.SafelistProtocolUtil containing the protocol-related helper methods previously implemented as private members of Safelist: getProtocolValue(Element, Attribute), isSafeProtocol(String, Set<Protocol>), and isValidAnchor(String). The new class will expose these as static methods so Safelist can call them. The new class will live in the same package org.jsoup.safety and include required imports (Element, Attribute, Set, TypedValue.Protocol, and the static lowerCase import).
Move the private method getProtocolValue(Element el, Attribute attr) from Safelist into SafelistProtocolUtil as a public static method with the same behavior.

Move the private method isSafeProtocol(String value, Set<Protocol> protocols) from Safelist into SafelistProtocolUtil as a public static method. The implementation is preserved, including the anchor handling and lowerCase usage.
Move the private static helper isValidAnchor(String value) into SafelistProtocolUtil as a private static method used by isSafeProtocol. (It remains package-private/static within the util class.)

Update internal calls in Safelist to reference the moved static methods on SafelistProtocolUtil. Specifically: replace getProtocolValue(el, attr) with SafelistProtocolUtil.getProtocolValue(el, attr) and replace isSafeProtocol(value, protocols) with SafelistProtocolUtil.isSafeProtocol(value, protocols). No external API changes are introduced; all public Safelist methods remain in place.

Add necessary imports to the new SafelistProtocolUtil: org.jsoup.nodes.Element, org.jsoup.nodes.Attribute, java.util.Set, org.jsoup.safety.TypedValue.Protocol, and the static import for org.jsoup.internal.Normalizer.lowerCase if used.

Update related tests affected by this refactoring block so the configured build command passes. Adjust imports, package references, moved class references, constructors, and assertions only when required. Do not change production behavior through tests.
